articleTitle: EMC Modeling and Simulation Codes
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Objective: The objective of the tutorial presentations is to provide overviews of the basics of numerical EMC analysis methods and associated codes. The tutorial shall give a short introduction and illustrate the technical aspects and applicability of the methods and codes.

articleTitle: The State-of-the-Art of ESD From the Design, Simulation, and the Advanced Technolgy Points of View
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This presentation will give an overview of the most recent trends in advanced CMOS technologies and discuss their impact on ESD protection design. The talk will then outline the latest concepts in advanced protection design and point out the need for effective simulation methods to optimize these ESD designs. Finally, the current limitations of the simulations tools and the requirements for an ideal simulator will be presented.

articleTitle: Workshop W2: New Measurement Techniques and Possible Future Standards in EMC
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This workshop will discuss a variety of new EMC measurement techniques and methods, and their possible impact on the development of specifications and standards. Included will be the following topics:

articleTitle: Demonstration of the Methodology
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Simulation of ESD devices includes process simulation as well as device simulation. It offers the advantages of reducing the number of silicon integrations as well as providing access to data that cannot be measured. The first checkpoint for process and device simulation consists in calibrating DC simulated curves with their measured counterparts. Once the calibrated simulation parameters are established, the ESD devices can be simulated in their operation mode (transient device simulation). A key issue are temperature effects and the corresponding models implemented in the device simulator. Besides the general simulation methodology, we also demonstrate the effect of small process variations as well as the influence of different thermal models on the performance of the ESD device.

articleTitle: Workshop W4: Electromagnetic Terrorism and Adverse Effects of High Power Electromagnetic (HPE) Environments
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Scientific, technical and practical aspects of intentional and unintentional use of high power electromagnetic environments. The importance to recognise these threats and risks in the context of information warfare and to create awareness. Methods to encounter possible effects.

articleTitle: Electrical Package Modeling Including Voltage and Ground Reference Planes Using the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) Method
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Proper decoupling of power and ground plane structures has been a subject of much controversy. Some EMC engineers believe proper decoupling design should be performed one way, and others will believe a different approach to decoupling design is best. Measurements of the effectiveness of different decoupling strategies is difficult and very time consuming. Today’s focus is on rapid product design, and the need to have an effective design the first time. It is important to be able to analyze decoupling design strategies rather than employing the trial and error process which is often used. The need to be able to simulate the effectiveness of decoupling design approaches is obvious. However, by it’s very nature, this type of analysis is difficult since it includes metal planes coupled to a large number of circuit elements. Many modeling techniques are not well suited to this type of problem. We show that the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) technique is useful for the solution of this type of problem. This paper describes work performed using PEEC to model large decoupling structures. Results show great promise for further work using PEEC for decoupling simulations.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Terrorism and Adverse Effects of High Power Electromagnetic Environments
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electromagnetic Terrorism is defined here as the intentional malicious generation of electromagnetic energy introducing noise or signals into electric and electronic systems, thus disrupting, confusing or damaging these systems for terrorist or criminal purposes. The electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) community which has significant experience in dealing with unintentional electromagnetic interference problems has a responsibility to deal with this problem and to set reasonable standards. Actors, pattern of action, and victims are described and examples of EM Terrorism given. Electromagnetic environment, consequences, protection, testing and assessment are discussed and a number of conclusions stated.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation Methods to Assess EM Terrorism Effects
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: HPM and UWB sources can represent a threat for the sensitive equipment of various military and civil targets. The paper focuses on effects on aircrafts and discusses the modeling possibilities available today to estimate such a threat for modern airplanes. An evaluation of voltages at the input of electronics, based on measured attenuations of a HPM field in a cavity and induced voltages in the wiring of a car which can be considered as being similar to the structure of an airplane cabling, is presented. This estimation shows the potential danger for the electronics submitted to a low level HPM.

articleTitle: Fast Susceptibility Analysis for Printed Circuit Boards Using an Equivalent-Wire Method of Moments
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The susceptibility analysis of printed circuit boards is presented as a new application of the method of moments in conjunction with a thin-wire equivalent model for the traces. This approach allows to determine voltages and currents induced within a complete trace net by an external interference field, with a minimum of computation and discretization effort. Arbitrary trace topologies can be treated. The external interference field is defined as a uniform plane wave with arbitrary polarization and direction of incidence. The presence of the dielectric substrate is fully accounted for by the combination of exact analytical expressions for the excitation field with a thin-wire Method of Moments formulation. Computational examples are presented and validated by accurate analytical results.

articleTitle: Statistical Description of Signal Propagation on Random Bundles of Wires
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The determination of disturbances in random cable bundles requires a statistical approach combined with the solution of non uniform transmission lines. The analysis of such a bundle of wires is typically performed in three steps: the generation of the bundle and its subdivision in a chain of uniform lines, the evaluation of the per-unit-length (p.u.l.) parameters in each cross section, and the solution of the line. In this paper, we propose a fractal generation of cables that is very fast and it is able to generate realistic cables by means of one tuning parameter. Line p.u.l. capacitances and inductances are evaluated through a very efficient implementation of the method of moments with Fourier expansion of the charge on conductors. The electrical simulation of the line is then performed via a chain matrix product of uniform sections. Since a statistical characterisation of a random non uniform line is extremely time consuming, Kriging method is adopted, because it is based on a very efficient fitting model that is able to describe the real situation with a limited number of simulations.

articleTitle: HPM Testing of a Car: A Representative Example of the Susceptibility of Civil Systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Based on rather comprehensive knowledge from HPM-testing of systems and components done in Sweden it is concluded that upset can be caused in unprotected electronic systems from a maximum distance of around 500 meters for an HPM source that can be located in a van. For a source of a smaller size, such that it can be located in a suitcase, the estimated distance decreases to 50 meters. The maximum distance for causing permanent physical damage is estimated to be around 15 meters for the HPM-van while the suitcase has to be placed very close to, or even in direct contact with, the target.

articleTitle: Theory and Modeling for EMC in Extended Systems : Current Capabilities and Requirements
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This document is an introductory reflection on the Technical Committee 7 (TC7) which focuses on theory and modeling of extended systems. A definition of extended systems is given in terms of a subsystem and multiple functions set. Then, what must be expected from models is discussed. Nowadays, the numerous existing models can solve very precise EMC problems but, from a user point of view, are not able to solve the whole system problem alone. The key answer of the analysis of the problem is certainly in an appropriate strategy to combine the existing tools.

articleTitle: ESD: What has been Achieved, What is Less Well Understood ?
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This introductory paper to the ESD session points at open questions and presents thoughts on measurement uncertainty calculation of ESD and tries to correct some misunderstanding on distance dependence of transient fields.

articleTitle: Optimization of the BLT Equation Based on a Sparse Gaussian Elimination
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This document presents the calculation time and the memory improvements obtained in the resolution of the EM Topology BLT equation when the sparse structure of the matrices is taken into account. The formalism is based on a classical Gaussian elimination, applied on blocks instead of scalars. It is shown how such a process is entirely equivalent to a successive compacting of junctions into others. This provides another improvement based on an efficient labeling of the waves on the networks. Results demonstrate the dramatic improvements obtained on different network topologies

articleTitle: Lightning Induced Voltages on Bare and Insulated Buried Cables
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In analysing the coupling mechanism between lightning electromagnetic fields and horizontally buried cables, there are two key parameters that have to be evaluated: the current and voltage propagation characteristics of the cable and the underground horizontal electric field that interacts with the cable. Several formulations to calculate the propagation constant and the lightning generated horizontal electric field at the depth of buried cable are available in the literature. However, not much studies that attempt to quantify the lightning induced voltages and currents in buried cables, taking into account both the distance of the lightning flash as well as the current in the return stroke channel, are available in the literature. In an attempt to fill this gap, a study was undertaken to evaluate the voltages induced in underground cables, with different lengths and with different characteristics (i.e. bare or insulated), when they are exposed to lightning generated electromagnetic fields. The Sunde’s formulation is used to obtain the propagation-constant of the cable. Results are presented for typical cable geometry (radius and dielectric thickness), typical soil characteristics (permitivity and conductivity) and for depths of burial that are of practical interest.

articleTitle: Measurement Uncertainties in EMC Instrumentation
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this workshop the subject of measurement uncertainty is discussed as an application of probability and statistics. These concepts will be presented from an intuitive rather than mathematical point of view. As an example the results will be applied to the measurement uncertainty due to instrumentation. This paper is only a summary of the actual workshop where the subject will be discussed in much more detail.

articleTitle: Diakoptics: An Efficient Technique for EMC Applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes a numerical procedure, called diakoptics, that allows one to solve for subdomains of a large structure in a rigorous manner. Hence, one can optimize such a subdomain during subsequent simulations without meshing the whole structure. This feature is very attractive for EMC applications that involve, for instance, shielding apertures. In addition, the technique is naturally well suited for Transmission-Line Matrix (TLM) computations. Although diakoptics is very demanding in terms of computer cost for three-dimensional (3D) cases, an accelerating procedure can substantially reduce the memory and CPU time requirement. Examples of applications related to shielding and radiation show the validity of the approach.

articleTitle: Wide-Band Total Radiated Power Measurements of Electronic Equipment in TEM and GTEM Cells
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper proposes an improvement to radiation measurements in TEM cells proposed by CISPR A and D in order to determine the total power radiated by electronic equipment. Based on previous theoretical work, the first part of this paper demonstrates that the individual voltages measured at each port of a TEM cell or on the single port of a GTEM cell respectively for three or six orientations of the equipment under test are sufficient to determine its total radiated power. The second part of this paper considers a practical industrial case where the wide-band total radiated power of an electronic equipment is measured in both TEM and GTEM cells. Finally, to highlight the repeatability and reproducibility of this method, a statistical analysis on 8 series of measurements combining different operators, different facilities and arbitrary initial orientations is presented.

articleTitle: Reduction of Complexity When Simulating Large-Scale PCB Circuits
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The simulation of large-scaled electronic circuits has its limits because of large amounts of data and long calculation times. This paper shows a way how to decrease the complexity of simulations by using screening effects. The method is explained on the Partial Elements Equivalent Circuit (PEEC)- method [6]-[9] used by modelling PCB’s and Power Supply Systems. Taking into consideration screening effects, systems with more than 120.000 Partial Elements can be handled.

articleTitle: Return-Stroke Radiation by a Branched Channel: A Transmission-Line Discharge Model
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper is concerned with the effects of branching in the lightning channel on the radiated fields of the return stroke. To model the current on the channel, we employ some recent results on the discharge of a transmission line that simulates the channel discharge. The effect of branches on the upward traveling return stroke pulse appears as a pulse-driven release of charge from the branch into the main channel. For the sake of simplicity, far-field radiation is obtained employing the modified transmission line (MTL) approximation for pulse propagation on the channel, which yields closed-form radiation.

articleTitle: An EMI Estimate for Shielding Enclosure Design
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A relatively simple, closed-form expression was developed to estimate the EMI from perforated shielding enclosures based on coupling from interior sources through slots and apertures at enclosure cavity modes [1], A power balance method [2], Bethe’s small hole theory [3], and empirically developed formulae for the relation between radiation and slot length and number of slots, were employed to estimate an upper bound on the radiated EMI from shielding enclosures. Comparisons between measurements and estimated field strengths suitably agree within engineering accuracy.

articleTitle: Influence of Electromagnetic Disturbances Induced on High Bit Rate Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Asymmetric Digital Subscriber Line (ADSL) is a new access technology which can provide a high bit rate digital channel by transmitting information over the existing installed twisted pairs of the access network. The quality of such transmission is of course affected by the non ideal transmission characteristics of the twisted pairs but also by electrical noise which is coupled into the cable from various sources. The aim of this paper is to determine the influence of impulse noise induced by an external electromagnetic wave on a ADSL transmission system. The first step leads to the calculation of the induced signals using a topology approach in conjunction with the transmission line theory. The effect of such electromagnetic disturbances on the transmission performance in terms of error rate is finally determined by using appropriate software.

articleTitle: Traceable Measurement of Horn Antenna Gain at Short Distances Using the„ 2½-Antenna-Method“
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A method for the traceable measurement of the short distance gain factor of horn antennas is described, based only on distance and attenuation measurements and an uncalibrated small field sensor. With an additional rf power measurement the field strength near the calibrated antenna may then be calculated.

articleTitle: Environmental EM Characterization
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Knowledge and control of the environmental electromagnetic field is an important topic for electromagnetic and EMC engineers and researchers. Environmental EM characterization is increasingly necessary to prevent humans from EM field exposure effects and electrical and electronic apparatus and systems from electromagnetic interference (EMI). The aim of this presentation is to focus some engineering aspects related to the analytical and experimental evaluation of electromagnetic fields generated by powerful low frequency and high frequency electromagnetic sources in the environment. Furthermore, a comparison between the reference levels of technical standards and Italian protection laws is presented and the precautionary principle is debated.

articleTitle: Advances in Antenna Calibration
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The major advances in antenna calibration presented in this session are (i) experimentally verified, precise calculations of height-dependent antenna factors of biconical antennas, (ii) methods for measurement and application of free-space antenna factors, (iii) a precise and traceable method for near-field calibrations of horn antennas, (iv) a novel method for the efficient determination of far-field patterns of directional antennas using microwave/infrared holography, and (v) a time-domain calibration method for EMP sensors.

articleTitle: Spread Spectrum Clocking and its Timing Impacts
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To meet FCC open-chassis emission regulation, it is necessary to suppress the radiation sources of PC systems. The technique of using Spread Spectrum Clocking (SSC) to reduce EMI is presented. SSC modulation profile, modulation frequency, and modulation amount are introduced. The timing impacts of SSC on a PLL-based system are discussed. Also given are the general requirements of PLL loop bandwidth frequency and phase angle of the input-to-output transfer function to minimize induced PLL tracking skew.

articleTitle: Optimising Mode Stirred Chambers
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Mode-Stirred chambers (over-moded degenerate cavities in which the electromagnetic field distribution is time varied) are traditionally associated with the military emc test environment, as they allow the susceptibility testing of vehicles and equipment in high intensity radiated fields (HIRF). They do this without raising environmental concerns and at a relatively low cost. The benefits of this low cost and flexibility make mode stirred chambers of increasing interest to commercial and research organisations. It is conventionally assumed that the resonant cavity, on which a mode-stirred facility is based should avoid mode degeneracy in order to maximise the efficiency of the facility. In this case, efficiency relates to the lowest frequency at which the chambers can be used with confidence. This paper analyses this presumption and concludes that latent degeneracy is not a specific issue providing that the level of “mode availability” is a primary design consideration. It outlines a design protocol to enable mode availability to be analysed.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling of EMC Problems using the TLM Method
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) Method is almost three decades old counting from its first introduction by P.B. Johns [1] in 1971. Since then the method has been proven to be a very powerful method for field computations in the time- and frequency-domain (2-4]. Originally based on the analogy between electromagnetic fields and transmission line voltages and currents [5], the TLM method has meanwhile been derived from Maxwell's equations using the finite difference approximation [6,7] and the method of moments [8]. As such it represents a full wave electromagnetic modeling tool with similar features as the finite difference time-domain (FDTD) method or it’s frequency-domain counterpart the (FD) method.

articleTitle: Measurement of Antenna Patterns Using Microwave/Infrared Holography
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the application of microwave holography to infrared (IR) thermographic images of electromagnetic (EM) fields for the purpose of measuring near-field and far-field radiation patterns of antennas. Microwave holography allows the recovery of the phase of the field from measured IR thermograms made of the magnitude of the fields. The phase can be extracted either (i) by an iterative Plane-to-Plane (P2P) two-dimensional (2D) Fourier Transformation method or (ii) from holographic interference patterns developed between the antenna-under-test (AUT) and a calibrated microwave antenna used as a reference standard. In either case, the near-field hologram data can be processed to determine the complex intensity (magnitude and phase) of the field at any distance in front of the AUT. Numerical simulations were performed to determine the feasibility, accuracy, and sensitivity of these IR holographic phase-retrieval techniques. The advantages and disadvantages of the two techniques are also compared.

articleTitle: Simulation of the Frequency Characteristics of Transmission Lines for Transient Calculations
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Equivalent circuits based on the telegrapher’s equations are suited for calculation of transient phenomena in transmission lines in the time domain. In order to simulate the frequency dependent properties of real lines, one-port networks are included in the equivalent circuit of each section. These proposed equivalent circuits give the possibility to calculate transients in transmission lines in the time domain, using responses of line parameters modified for high frequencies. Different approaches for the determination of the lines one-port network equivalent parameters simulating this frequency dependence of per unit length line parameters are considered. The results of such an approach for the analysis of fast processes in systems with small losses are affected by oscillations caused by the imperfections of the mathematical model of the line. An approach permitting to damp these oscillations and to increase the accuracy and efficiency of the transient calculations is proposed and justified.. The method is based on an artificial increase of losses in the line in a range of frequencies not essential for a valid reproduction of the transient process.

articleTitle: Use of Nuclear Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Simulators for Protection of Civil Systems Against Other Electromagnetic Threats
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: During the Cold War, the United States, the Soviet Union, and several other countries built large test facilities to ensure that critical military systems would continue to function in the event of intense electromagnetic pulses created by high-altitude nuclear explosions. Many of these mammoth test facilities, developed at large expense to the national defense budgets, have been decommissioned or sit idle as a result of successful EMP hardening of these military systems and the end of the Cold War. However, the nuclear EMP threat has not gone away, and new EM threats have emerged. Some of these test facilities could be useful as tools for hardening civil electronic systems against such new electromagnetic threats as terrorist use of high-power microwave or ultra-wideband radiating systems. Subcommittee 77C of the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) plans to develop a compendium of technical information about worldwide EMP simulators that have applicability for electromagnetic compatibility tests in general as well as these new electromagnetic threats.

articleTitle: Measurement of the Break-Down Voltage in a Very-Small Gap Discharge
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: It is examined whether a discharge occurs or not at the applied voltage of less than 330V and at a few micro meters gap length by measuring a discharge currents and an electric fields. As a result, a discharge occurs at the applied voltage of less than 330V in the gap length of less than 4μm contrary to the Paschen’s law in both cases of the approaching electrode and the fixed electrode.

articleTitle: Cost Effective EMC Verification Testing in the Satellite Industry
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In previous years satellite development was dominated by technical achievement and not cost control. Today cost control is one of the primary drivers for both scientific and commercial satellite projects. Past traditions and practices have to be abandoned to find more cost effective solutions in order to remain competitive. EMC verification tests are one of the areas where costs can be significantly reduced without compromising safety margins if the right measures are taken. This paper describes how a practical approach lowered the verification test costs by 50% in a satellite development program.

articleTitle: A Partitioning Based Approach for a Card in Enclosure Problem
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The solution of electromagnetic problems of an ever increasing size is of importance for the design of new products in both the EMI and the EIP (Electrical Interconnect and Package) analysis. Today, conventional techniques do not have the capacity to solve complex heterogeneous problems of a realistic size. In this paper we suggest that partitioning based techniques can be of great help in the solution of EMI problems for realistic computer packages. In particular a systematic methodology is given for the partitioned solution of a realistic computer package structure which involves printed circuit cards as well as the computer enclosure.

articleTitle: A New Radio Frequency Absorber for GTEM Cell Applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Different types of EMC testing sites (TEM, GTEM Cells) and various materials and structures used as radio frequency absorbers are summarised. Then a new type cellular structure radio frequency absorber is presented which has several advantages compared to the usual large, expensive pyramid absorbers. Some measurement results (reflection versus frequency characteristic) and a short description of an experimental GTEM chamber with this new absorber are also given.

articleTitle: A New Method to Evaluate the Impulse Responses of Lossy Multiconductor Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the evaluation of the time-domain describing input and transfer impulse responses of linear lossy multiconductor transmission lines with frequency dependent parameters. These responses cannot be evaluated analytically and, due to the presence of “irregular” terms such as Dirac pulses, a brute numerical evaluation is not possible. In this paper an analytical method based on the perturbation theory of the spectrum of symmetric matrices is applied to evaluate exactly all the irregular terms. Once the irregular parts of the impulse responses are known, it is possible to evaluate accurately the regular ones through simple numerical methods, as shown through some examples.

articleTitle: A New Earth Resistance Measurement Method Using a Resonant Circuit
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, a new earth resistance measurement technique has been proposed. The technique is to evaluate an earth resistance for earth electrode by measuring the loop impedance at the resonant frequency, which consists of impedances for the earth electrode, return metallic plane and lead wires. From theoretical and experimental results, it was found that the earth resistance of earth electrode can be obtained by the loop impedance at the resonant frequency. Some experimental results showed good agreements with those of the conventional measurement method.

articleTitle: Exposure Systems and their Dosimetry 7th COST 244bis MCM and 6th Workshop in Zurich, Switzerland
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: COST stands for European Cooperation in the Field of Scientific and Technical Research. It is financed by the European Union and functions as a framework for scientific and technical cooperation of national research on a European level. Apart from the fifteen EU member states COST has ten members more, i.e. Croatia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Iceland, Norway, Slovakia, Slovenia, Switzerland, Turkey and the European Commission. The activities of COST appear as “COST Actions”. All COST member countries can propose a COST Action or participate in an existing one by signing the corresponding Action Memorandum of Understanding.

articleTitle: The Influence of Speed of Approach and Humidity on the Intensity of ESD
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: ESD may be a serious threat to electronic devices and systems. The intensity of ESD can vary strongly in spite of constant charge voltage. The bad reproducibility of ESD is notorious. The most influencing factors of an ESD are the discharge geometry, the materials, the charge voltage and the arc length. A statistically changing arc length is the reason for strong variations of the intensity of discharges. E.g. the current amplitude may vary up to two orders of magnitude due to different arc lengths. The arc length is a difficult to handle parameter, therefore it is desirable to know on which more obvious and better observable parameters the arc length and so the intensity depends on. Some of the most influencing parameters of the arc length are the speed of approach and the ambient humidity. Subject of this paper is to introduce a new method to simulate ESD that considers the statistical nature of ESD. With this method the intensity of ESD depending on important parameters could be determined. Detailed results were presented.

articleTitle: EMC in Railway Systems: Conductive Coupling From Track to Nearby Metallic Structures
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Conductive coupling from a typical Norwegian railway system containing booster transformers to a parallel telephone cable is studied. Relevant input data are provided, and some verifying measurements are performed. Good agreement between calculated and measured earth potentials support the methods used, but further studies of the coupling are considered necessary.

articleTitle: Statistical Considerations on Electrical Fast Transient/Burst Immunity Tests
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An analytical approach is presented which describes some relevant features at the output of an EFT/B test. Since the result of this test is affected by the random timing between the applied disturbance and the EUT’s susceptibility, the analysis is developed also taking into account the right statistical aspects. Explicit expressions are given for the quantities that measure the impact of bursts on the EUT behavior, like the number of sensitive susceptible windows and the power spectral densities. This way, one has some tools to predict the efficiency of the test, and to adjust the set-up arrangement, in such a way as to be sure that the most significant operation conditions are actually explored.

articleTitle: A Procedure for Evaluating the Reflectivity Level of Anechoic Chambers Based on Numerical Simulations
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work a novel method for the evaluation of reflectivity level in anechoic chambers is proposed. It is based on the use of measurements of electric field in the chamber (produced and then received by two identical dipoles) and numerical simulations (of the two dipoles in free space) with FDTD algorithm. In a series of points in a volume of interest in the chamber, measurements give the field as a composition of direct and reflected field, whereas numerical simulations give the direct field (with no reflections). The difference between these values gives the contribution of reflections in the chamber.

articleTitle: Experimental Description of Electromagnetic Coupling Occurring on Transmission Lines at High Frequencies (300MHz-10GHz)
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In most cases of electromagnetic coupling to transmission lines, hypothesis of infinite ground plane and TEM approximation are considered. Induction to the lines or the estimation of radiation due to the currents distribution are explained by coupled transmission line theory .The proposed article consists of explaining certain experiments carried out in anechoic chamber and MSRC in which the assumptions of infinite ground plane and the application of transmission line theory will not be wholly justified at extremely high frequencies(above 2GHz). Interpretation of certain observed physical phenomena will also be proposed to compare the radiation of the devices with a short monopole.

articleTitle: Lightning Electric and Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Characteristics of measured electric and magnetic fields generated by various lightning processes are reviewed. Ground flashes of both polarities and cloud flashes are considered. Examples of different types of field waveforms are given.

publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: • Maxwell’s Equations - a practical guide: Basic FDTD formulation• Material interfaces in FDTD • Dielectrics • Metals • Wires and other sub-cell elements • Dispersive dielectrics, ferrites, active elements etc • Virtual measurements. Extracting information from FDTD • SAR computations • Quasi-static formulation of FDTD • Direct illustration of laws and phenomena • Virtual measurements • Available commercial codes. Comparison • Conclusions

articleTitle: A Stochastic Approach for Determining the Reverberating Chamber Quality Factor
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A simple and effective stochastic approach for determining the reverberating chamber quality factor is presented. It is based on the averaged periodogram and permits to characterize the spectral behavior of the electromagnetic field within the reverberating chamber. Indeed two basic parameters can be determined: the reverberating chamber quality factor Q, and the bandwidth enlargement factor Δf. Such a characterization can be of valuable aid for designing and testing a reverberating chamber as well as for the comparability of different ones.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Radiated Lightning Coupling on Real MV Power Lines by an EMP Simulator
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A real size, real configuration Medium Voltage (MV) power distribution line has been tested under a large, vertically polarised Electro-Magnetic Pulse (EMP) simulator. The reproducible incident fields permitted a better estimation and prediction of the coupling to power and terminal components (e.g. transformers) than an actual lightning pulse. The transient propagation on real power line and real ground earth has been also verified during the test campaign. A parallel activity dedicated to simulation of the field-to-line coupling was performed, using models based both on classic Transmission Line Theory (EMTP tool) and on numeric methods (NEC tool). Finally, a full simulation of the large EMP facility and of the MV line under test was performed with an advanced EMC predictor (EMC2000 tool).

articleTitle: Theoretical Investigation of Automotive Emissions Measurements at 3 m and 10 m Ranges
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Although automotive emissions measurements are conventionally carried out at a range of 10 m under semi-anechoic conditions, some standards permit measurements at 3 m to be used if a 10 dB adjustment is applied to the limit. Electromagnetic modelling has been employed to investigate this approach, and to assess whether data recorded in a fully anechoic environment can be used in this manner. This work indicates that measurements at 3 m can provide more accurate electric field data and that the effect of the ground plane is small at this range. These studies also suggest that a 5 dB adjustment may be more appropriate to estimate 10 m levels.

articleTitle: EMC-Based Lightning Protection Concept: Surge Protection in Existing Structures
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Lightning Protection Zones (LPZ)-Concept shows measures against Lightning Electromagnetic Impulses (LEMP). This report emphasizes the requirements of a surge protection system against conducted surge currents for the special conditions of existing structures. • The special conditions for surge protection in existing structures are described in this paper. • Guidelines to realize surge protection systems in existing structures are given. • The efficiency of surge protection systems in existing structures is proven by computer simulations.

articleTitle: Complexed Probabilistic-Statistical Evaluation of Civil Aerotechnics Electromagnetic Compatibility and Safety
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Based on results of analysis of the typical electromagnetic environment (EME) in airports and on civil airways, are offered classification of the typical EME and are substantiated the general technical requirements of the civil aerotechnics electromagnetic compatibility and safety (EMC/S). On that basis are created conception and methodology of the complexed probabilistic-statistical evaluation of the civil aerotechnics EMC/S, that had been practical realized for the first time in M.M.Gromov Flight Research Institute (FRI). Also hardware and software support of the complexed EMC/S-evaluation during development, the certification tests and operation of civil aerotechnics are briefly presented. With that end in view, in M.M.Gromov FRI with participation of Institute of Electronics (Minsk city) were for a last decade carried out the theoretical and experimental researches of the abovementioned EMC/S-problems, development of conception and methodology, hardware and software support of the complexed probabilistic-statistical evaluation of the civil aerotechnics EMC/S at all stages of its life cycle (development, tests and operation), also its proofing and introduction in practice of the certificaton tests of the new civil aerotechnics [3-7]. Principal results of these works for the first time are for the foreign forum briefly presented in the given paper.

articleTitle: Effects of the Presence of a Human Operator on the Folded Loop Antenna for Mobile Hand-Held Units
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electromagnetic interaction between handset-mounted antennas and the human body is of particular importance for cellular telephones and hand-held terminals of other “personal-oriented” wireless communications systems. This paper presents the results of analysis of the influence of the user’s head on the radiation patterns and input impedance of the vertical wire folded loop antenna mounted on a conducting box simulating the hand-held mobile device. The numerical analysis is performed by the finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method. A simple three-layered spherical head model is employed. The results reveal that the user’s head significantly affects the antenna radiation patterns, whereas the antenna input impedance is influenced to much lesser degree.

articleTitle: EMC-Aspects of Industrial Data Communication Networks
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Minor EMC-failures in industrial process control networks may have severe safety and cost implications due to possible accidents and production loss. Apart from (legal) emission and immunity equipment requirements, the correct implementation of EMC-cabling measures in the field is particularly critical. This paper describes the major EMC aspects of industrial data communication networks, based on EMI-trouble shooting experience in more than twenty process control installations, ranging from (petro)chemical plants and paper production lines to food processing industry. A step-bystep trouble shooting procedure is presented and a summary of EMC-installation measures is given.

articleTitle: A Cascade of Tapered Transmission Lines for the Lightning Return-Stroke Modeling
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The model here presented is based on the representation of the lightning channel by a cascade of nonuniform lossless transmission lines, whose parameters are in function of height, according to an exponential law. Each block of the line cascade is characterized by a suitable exponential law so that the propagation velocity holds constant. The analysis is carried out in the s-domain and available algorithms are adopted for the numerical inverse Laplace transform. The model gives both the current distribution along the discharge channel and the radiating field on the soil surface. The results are in good agreement with the experimental evidences.

articleTitle: Non-Gaussian Signals Separation VIA Higher-Order Statistics and Adaptive Filtering
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The background to non-Gaussian signals (definitions, classification, treatment) - from a telecommunication point of view - has been done. A particular case of inter - symbol interference was considered in detail. It is shown that a heavy interfered signals (ISI up to 50% ) can be recovered to original form using HOS and adaptive filtering. A comparison of lattice to transversal filters is attached.

articleTitle: Bioelectromagnetics: The Gap Between Scientific Knowledge and Public Perception
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Biological effects of electromagnetic fields (EMF) have been studied since decades. Based on this well established scientific base, exposure guidelines for the general public and workers have been proposed by many renowned institutions. Based on these proposals, several countries have introduced regulations and legislation to protect workers and the general public form excessive exposure to EMF. Some of these government regulations on EMF exposure include additional precautions to avoid possibly unknown long term effects. However, the fact is, that the available scientific base on biological interactions of EMF does not allow clear conclusions in regard of chronic effects. This may be a reason why the public attention in several countries is focused on the question of possible long term effects from modem wireless communication systems. The main reason of this increased public attention is the massive roll-out of cellular telephone systems in most industrialised countries making a large amount of EMF sources visible.

articleTitle: Activity of URSI Commission E Working Group: E-7 on Extraterrestrial and Terrestrial Meteorologico-Electric Environment With Noise and Chaos
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This article reviews the progress made recently by URSI Working Group E-7 (Chairman: H. Kikuchi; Co-Chairman: S.S. Moiseev) on Extraterrestrial and Terrestri Meteoroiogico-Electric Environment with Noise and Chaos. The topics covered are: cosmic dusty plasmas; laboratory dusty plasmas; gravito-electrodynamics; EHD and EMHD; self-organization and chaos; terrestrial lightning; planetary lightning; nebular lightning; ball lightning; cloud-to-ionosphere discharges; tomadie thunderstorms; pre-earthquake effects of dust; terrestrial (ionospheric and magnetospheric) noise; extraterrestrial and cosmic noise.

articleTitle: A MoM Solution for the Efie Applicable to Any Combination of Thin-Wire and Surface Scatterers Down to Low Frequencies
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The Method of Moments (MoM) has been so far, due to limited computer code precision, restrained to the resonance region. A generalized set of basis and test functions, which decouple the problem into a magnetostatic and an electrostatic one, is presented here. Their application, that implies very modest additional computational effort, enables the Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) to be solved by the MoM from the resonance region until extremely low frequencies. Further, the treatment of the geometry as a graph enables the automatic application of the methodology to any combination of thin-wire and surface scatterers, without any necessity of special basis functions. The methodology is validated by analytical calculations and applied to determine the attenuation of a metal housing at 50 Hz.

articleTitle: EMC-Aspects of Resistance Welding Machines
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The knowledge of emissions is important for the evaluation of risks occuring by use of electrical machines in their environment. Technical systems are influenced by high-frequency noise voltages and electromagnetic fields. Furthermore effects of magnetic fields on biological systems are described. The results of measurements of conducted and radiated emissions as well as magnetic field measurements of different resistance welding machine types are presented in the following paper.

articleTitle: Results of a Round Robin Test Performed in Different Automotive EMC Vehicle Chambers
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper gives a presentation and an analysis of the results obtained with a round robin test performed in six different EMC vehicle chambers in Europe. First, a calibration field level measurement was performed in each facility according to the prescriptions of the automotive EMC directive 95/54/EC [1] and also according to ISO 11451-2 (1990) [2] and its future amendment]. Only the narrow band immunity tests were considered. A comparison and a statistical analysis of the calibrated field levels used in each facility, for a one-sensor substitution method, is presented and shows that the uncertainties are not so important when considering the large number of different parameters. The new four-sensor method included in the revised version of the ISO 11451-2 standard was also implemented. Experimental results are shown to illustrate the comparison of both methods. A study of the calibration of the electric field sensors themselves used in each facility was finally performed, in order to evaluate their direct influence on the results.

articleTitle: Development of a Practical Optical Electric Field Sensor in GHz Range
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: We have developed a compact optical electric field sensor in the GHz range integrating an optical modulator and an antenna using a segmented electrode structure in a chip. The 3dB baseband range is 4.95 GHz. The minimum detectable field is lower than 80 dBMV/m (BW=1kHz). And this sensor is stable in temperature cycle test (-20 ∼ 60 °C) and heat shock test ( Δ T>60 °C ). The package size of the fabricated sensor head is as small as 75 × 11 × 6.5 mm. Therefore, it is portable and can be used in measuring at various places, such as near the relay antenna of the cellular phone on the street and in the dummy of the human head.

articleTitle: Effect of Wire Radii Tolerances on Differential to Common Mode Conversion in Balanced Twisted Pairs
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The hypothesis that the differential to common-mode conversion in twisted pairs is originated by the small difference in the wire diameters is investigated. Results show that the investigated mechanism produces the observed behavior. A thorough test of the presented theory is proposed as further study.

articleTitle: Transients: Measurement, Simulation and Protection
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Transients are of special interest concerning the susceptibility of electronic systems. Transients with steep edges show comparatively large frequency spectra. In most cases transient interferences are characterized by peak values which are much higher than the signal amplitudes on lines. A special class of transients is represented by HPM pulses (HPM: High Power Microwave). In order to investigate the coupling of transients to electronic structures or electronic components respectively as well as to measure the susceptibility of electronic equipment against transients special simulators (generators in combination with suitable antenna systems) have to be developed. By application of interfering transients, showing severe values, not only disturbances of system functions but also destructions or irreversible variations of system parameters respectively may occur. These transients have to be attenuated or suppressed respectively by special nonlinear protection circuits (filters) in order to guarantee a faultless system operation. The filter parameters depend on the values provided by the susceptibility measurements. Besides measurements computer modeling as well as computer simulations, which enable predictions of transient field coupling, have to be carried out.

articleTitle: Topics in EMC Innovation
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the first part of the paper the goals of the session EMC INNOVATION are described; in the second part the scientific contributions presented are briefly summarized.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Interference Induced on a Transmission Line by an Electrostatic Discharge Inside Metallic Enclosures
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A lot of well documented operation anomalies, but also many catastrophic failures on board of orbiting spacecraft are due to electrostatic discharge (ESD). Moreover, the evolution of the electronic systems is leading to a denser packaging and to the use of lower intensity signals, increasing in this way the susceptibility of the electronic equipment. Therefore an accurate design is necessary to protect the circuitry from the effects of a broad band disturbing field due to an ESD, but this can be achieved when effective simulation tools are available. In this sense, this paper presents a model for the evaluation of the disturbance induced in a transmission line by an ESD occurring inside a metallic enclosure, representing the metallic shield of an apparatus. The model highlights the effects of the resonant nature of the structure on the intensity and on the duration of the disturbance; theoretical results have been validated by measurements.

articleTitle: Analysing Link Performance in High Frequency Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Link performance in data transmission systems working at high frequencies is analysed. Transmission Line Model (TLM) is used for the simulation of a twisted pair cable connected to a voltage source and a resistive load and linked through two pin connectors. Using this model, the total Return Loss (RL) of the transmission system (Connector-Cable-Connector), and the total attenuation (a) is determined. The effect of the variation of the characteristic impedance of both connectors on the link performance is investigated. Results indicate that significant care and attention should be given when choosing cable connectors in such high speed systems. This paper concludes with an indication of the advantages of using the modelling approach over purely analytical or experimental approaches.

articleTitle: Validation of a Hybrid MoM-MTL Method Calculating Complex Structures on PCBs
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with a coupling of the calculation method using the Multiconductor Transmission Line (MTL) equation and the Method of Moments (MoM). An algorithm base on a single-wire TL and MoM presented in [1] was extended by use of MTL to account for more realistic structures such as multiple coupled lines, e.g. bus structures, cable bundles etc. For a reasonable application it is nessesary to divide the disposition into parts calculated either by MTL or MoM depending on the geometry. The coupling of the methods is then considered by an iterative algorithm which utilizes an integral for the electrical field strength. The hybrid method is used to calculate the currents and electromagnetic fields of a PCB. It is shown that the results are in close agreement to the measured values of the PCB.

articleTitle: Presentation of a Hybrid Code for EMC Simulation of Electronic Boards
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents an innovative concept of « direct » coupling of a three-dimensional time Boundary Element Method electromagnetism code with a Spice type electrical simulator well known to electronic engineers. This « hybrid » type code is very useful for the ElectroMagnetic Compatibility (E.M.C.) study of electronic boards or components. Therefore, we present mainly the two existing types of coupling, labeled «indirect» and «direct» respectively. For « direct » coupling corresponding to the « hybrid code » it will be shown that rules are respected to guarantee convergence of this coupling during each time step.

articleTitle: A Test Method for Immunity of Radio-Linked Automation Systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper presents a test method for radiolink used in automation systems; it is based on the injection, into the receiver input, of a signal equivalent to that produced by an electromagnetic field impinging on the antenna of the receiver itself. The test can be performed without using the anechoic chamber and by means of low power amplifier, resulting in a very low cost technique, with respect to the standard aims (EN 61000-4-1). Beside the standard CW and modulated signal, the interference produced by a cellular phone (GSM) have been used to verify the performance degradation of a LABMATE robot, showing an interesting example of out of band audio rectification.

articleTitle: New Frequency-Dependent Models for Close-Spaced Multiwire Lines Oyer a Conducting Plane
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electrical systems are often interconnected by wires arranged over ground or over a conducting plane. The paper highlights the importance of proximity effect consideration. Matrix impedances and admittances of very close spaced conductors over a ground plane are determined. The proposed model has been evaluated in a wide frequency range and compared to the case in which skin effect alone is considered. The results obtained are in good agreement with expectations. The model can obviously complete existing analytical models, which often neglect proximity effects.

articleTitle: Radiation From a Traction Line Due to Arcs Between a Pantograph and the Contact Wire
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The electric arc produced between sliding board of the pantograph and contact wire and the related current propagating along the railway line is modelled; the model is based on a non linear integro-differential system of two equations where the unknowns are represented by the arc current and by the non linear arc conductance. The model is used to predict the electromagnetic field radiated by the line and the results are compared with experimental data.

articleTitle: An Optically Linked Three-Loop Antenna System for Determining the Near Field Characteristics from an Electrically Small Source
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility

articleTitle: A Proper Framework for EMC Standards
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new and proper framework for EMC requirements and standards is presented in this paper. From a fundamental point of view the environment of use is stated as the first item in the selection process; The manufacturer has to choose the environment in which the product can function within its specifications. Product specific aspects should be abandoned in EMC standards to limit the vast increasing number of standards. The consistency in test methods could be improved by making emission and immunity test set-ups at least reversible and well defined.

articleTitle: New Developments in Computational Electromagnetics for EMC Problems
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The complexity of todays EMC problems requires sophisticated numerical techniques to model electromagnetic fields accurately. However, since rigorous field computation techniques are typically time-consuming, lumped element representations are still attractive to achieve fast and, for a limited application range, reasonably accurate solutions. In this session we present a combination of papers reporting advances in existing numerical techniques as well as in the development of equivalent and lumped element approximations of EM fields.

articleTitle: Measurements for ESD Coupling Model Validation
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A correct measurement of electrostatic discharges (ESD) effects requires not only an adequate instrumentation, but also a thought experimental set-up, especially when the measurements are used to validate theoretical models of the ESD coupling mechanisms. Due to the transient nature of the ESD, the signals induced on the victim circuit are acquired in the time domain using large bandwidth oscilloscope: the required bandwidth depends upon the resonant frequencies of the victim structure itself. Particular care must be devoted, during the experiment, to avoid the effects of unwanted coupling mechanisms, different from those modelled. The paper presents several cases of conducted and radiated coupling, with the set-up description and the comparison with theoretical models.

articleTitle: Modeling and Simulation in Multiconductor Transmission Line Theory
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Multiconductor transmission lines (MTLs) are an indispensable part in the treatment of complex BMC problems. A numerical model for transmission lines can be based to a large extent on analytical solutions. This has the great advantage that computing time is reduced. Usually analytical solutions for uniform and nonuniform MTLs are incorporated in the analysis of networks of different kinds. This may be networks occurring in Electromagnetic Topology on the basis of a generalized BLT equation as well as usual networks with lumped elements, including nonlinear ones. Our representation is divided into two parts: The first part deals with EM-Topology, invented by Baum, Liu and Tesche, and further developed by Parmantier et al. The second one includes nonuniform MTLs into a network analysis which roots in contributions from Singer et al. We begin with EM-Topology, explaining the breakdown of a complex electromagnetic problem into several smaller problems, using an aircraft which is excited from outside. Topological and interaction graphs for the different coupling steps from outside to inside the system are described, finally resulting into a very general structure equation (the generalized BLT equation). In this equation two supermatrices play an important role: the scattering- and propagation-supermatrices. It is emphasized that the junction characterization with the aid of the scattering matrix can be performed with various methods, e.g. MoM, FDTD, analytical solutions or experiments, to name only a few of those methods. On the other hand, the tube characterization to obtain the propagation matrix still takes place in the framework of MTL theory. But also in this context more generalized ansaetze are in preparation. The solution of the BLT equation with the CRIPTE code applied to an example concludes the first part of our paper. In the second part of our presentation we focus on the treatment of nonuniform MTLs in time- and frequency domain network simulations. In both cases the solution of the telegrapher equations are used to establish equivalent networks. In time domain controlled current sources are added to the network at both ends of the lines, whereas in frequency domain the line is taken into account by a two-port with three impendances in Π- arrangement. A generalized Bergeron-procedure is applied to calculate lossy and nonuniform lines in time-domain. In frequency-domain the matrizant approximation for nonuniform MTLs is related to the corresponding chain matrix of the line which in turn is used as basis to estimate the ingredients of the equivalent network. Examples in both domains are studied and serve as elucidation of our procedure.

articleTitle: A Comparison of Methods to Evaluate RF Absorbers Between 30 MHz and 500 MHz Before and aFter Installation
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Monostatic and bistatic methods to measure the reflection coefficient in semi or fully anechoic chambers are are explained. Their principal abilities and practical results are compared for the frequency range of 30 MHz to 500 MHz.

articleTitle: The Method of Moments (MOM) and Related Codes
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Integral equation methods have proved to be powerful tools for the numerical computation of electromagnetic fields. Among the integral equation methods the method of moments (MOM) is frequently used for the analysis of EMC problems. In this contribution the mathematical basis and the principle of the MOM are introduced. Meanwhile many MOM variants exist, concerning e.g. the formulation of the integral equation (EFIE, MFIE, CFIE, ...) or concerning modeling by means of thin-wire structures using line-current sources or with surface structures applying surface currents and discretization by quadrangular or triangular surface patches. The tutorial lesson will treat some of these variants. It is also shown how to analyze dielectric materials. In the MOM it is required to solve an equation system with a fully occupied matrix, and problems of industrial applications can lead to many thousands of unknowns. Therefore it can be advantageous to choose an iterative method instead of Gauss elimination or LU decomposition to solve the equation system. The contribution gives some recommendations for modeling and computation, concerning computer storage and frequency-dependent segmentation. The conditions for thin-wire simulations are shown as well as some modeling requirements when conductors are simulated by surface patches. Some remarks on possible checks concerning the validity of the solution follow. A comparison of the MOM with differential equation approaches shows that the MOM offers a lot of advantages. Particularly favorable is the MOM when exterior problems (open geometries) have to be treated, and when only few different, linear and homogeneous media are considered. In the EMC practice there are many applications of this type, for instance radiation from short-wave antennas, far-field evaluations like radiation diagrams, or coupling through apertures out of or into enclosures. As will be shown in the contribution the MOM is very suitable for hybridizing with analytical and numerical procedures like GTD/UTD. When combining with analytical methods, e.g. transmission line theory, a lot of sophisticated tasks can be solved, e.g. precise and reliable computation of high values of shielding effectiveness or coupling into shielded cables. In contrast to the FDTD method or the FEM, the MOM requires only a surface gridding, therefore the expenditure for gridding is relatively low. In the tutorial lecture some codes which are based on the MOM are quoted. Finally, some examples which have been treated by means of the MOM illustrate the applicability of this method.

articleTitle: Susceptibility of Car Radios to Ignition Noise
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In-car receivers are susceptible to impulsive noise, as generated by the vehicle’s ignition system. The interference not only enters the radio via the antenna directly, but also via the supply leads or can result from a poor grounding structure. Efficient and low cost interference suppression can be achieved only in cases where the interference coupling mechanism is clearly understood. This paper presents a practical methodology, based on simple tools, enabling users to find the dominant interference coupling mechanism. The interference methodology presented is focused on ignition noise in the AM (LW+MW) and FM reception bands.

articleTitle: Design and Testing of Partially Lined Screened Rooms
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes the design and measurements that have been made on a partially lined screened room. The design described uses ferrite tiles to implement the partial lining technique described by Dawson and Marvin. Dawson has devised TLM (Transmission Line Matrix) modelling code so that damping levels can be predicted prior to application of the lining. The paper describes how the code was used to arrive at the end design. This includes a description of how modelling of a biconical antenna, broadband noise source and ferrite tiles were undertaken. Graphs of both measured and predicted performance are presented. Measurements of site attenuation of the partially lined chamber with respect to EN 50147-2. and CENELEC report R110-003 are also given.

articleTitle: Simulation of Conducted Electromagnetic Interference of Inverter-Fed Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The present paper deals with the development of a simulation method for conducted electromagnetic interference produced by inverter-fed induction motors. Power electronic systems generate impulse currents through the power leads causing serious electromagnetic interference problems. In the proposed approach the dominant emission sources are identified. A model of the spreading path of the noises is developed. For EMI simulation parasitics of devices and board layout have to be considered. One approach to shorten the modeling process is to replace parts of the system by measurement results. Results of the simulations and further possibilities are discussed.

articleTitle: On the Relation Between Radiated and Conducted RF Emission Tests
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper deals with the RF emission from small electronic products with a single (mains) cable in the frequency range from 30 to 230 MHz. Because it is important to have EMC assessments in an early stage of the product development, there is a need for simple, low-cost test methods that can be applied in the design lab. A workbench set-up, as described in IEC 61000-46, which is primarily intended for RF immunity testing, is also suitable for conducted RF emission testing. The relation between conducted and radiated test results is discussed and special attention is paid to systematic measurement uncertainties that may occur in both setups. A simple theoretical relation is derived, which corresponds well to the relation obtained from measurements, provided that the resonance effects in the radiated set-up are suppressed, e.g. by applying a common mode termination impedance to the cable.

articleTitle: A Multiconductor Transmission Line Method to Study Non-Perfect Ground Planes
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In most cases of electrical structures a ground plane is present. The modeling of this kind of conductor is usually achieved considering it is perfect and using the image method. This modeling becomes often not sufficient for small or massive planes. In this paper the Multi-conductor Transmission Lines method is applied to study a basic case of a non-perfect ground plane (including of course propagation effects). Results of complete modeling are compared to measurements.

articleTitle: On the Measurement of EMC in Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper describes a selection of methods applied to the measurement of electromagnetic emission and susceptibility of integrated circuits. Although some of the methods are still in an experimental phase, most of the measurement techniques presented in the following paper are becoming standards at international level. The radio frequency immunity and the emission measurement methods are reviewed, described and compared.

articleTitle: Using GTEM-Cells for Time Domain Measurements
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The paper describes a method to calculate the time-dependent currents in an emission source of simple design from the time-dependent output voltages, measured with a digital oscilloscope at the GTEM-cell. The measured voltages in time domain must be transformed into the frequency domain. A complex multipole correlation procedure, containing magnitude and phase information, allows to determine the complex electric and magnetic moments. These can be transformed into the time domain to calculate the currents that cause the emissions.

articleTitle: Measurement Technology Developments in Test Methods and Environment
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radiated immunity and emission tests are the subject of this session. The development of new test methods and facilities is driven by the need of reducing time and cost of testing improving at the same time the quality of measurement results in terms of both repeatability (among measurements) and reproducibility (among laboratories).

articleTitle: Overview and Recent Progress for the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) Method
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Today, the requirements for the EMC analysis of modern electronic equipment are very challenging. The hardware to be modeled is becoming more complex and the frequency ranges of interest are continuously increasing. This makes both the design of such equipment as well the EMC analysis more difficult. In this tutorial we give an outline of the Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) technique for the solution of such problems. This method is a circuit based technique for the hybrid electromagnetic and circuit problems. Further, we will talk about some of the recent innovations in the method, since the PEEC method and models are continuously evolving to meet new challenges. We also give some examples of problems which have been solved with this approach.

articleTitle: Observation of Lightning Discharge Processes using Broadband Radio Interferometer
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A broadband radio interferometer, one of the sophisticated techniques to reveal the mechanism of lightning discharges, has been designed and tested by authors and it gave us useful results on locating sources of electromagnetic radiation from lightning discharges and reconstructing lightning discharge channels. The advantage of this technique is the capability of positioning radiation sources for both isolated pulses and pulse bursts. A single-station lightning location experiment using radio interferometer has been carried out in Darwin, Australia in December 1997. One of the experimental result shows a series of strokes occurred in a negative cloud to ground discharge. Radiation of cloud discharge activities was also recorded during the early stages of initial and subsequent leaders to ground. The subsequent leaders have the same channel path with the first leader. Period of this cloud to ground flash was in the range of hundred milliseconds. The location of radio frequency sources emitted from lightning is drawn both in two dimensions map and in time sequences.

articleTitle: Efficient Time Domain Modeling of E.M. Coupling Between Metallic Enclosures
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In many Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) problems we have to deal with interacting objects of arbitrary shape placed in the same environment. The interaction among different equipments is particularly strong in presence of transient phenomena.
