In this contribution, we model the e.m. field of interacting objects in the time domain by means of a hybrid Transmission Line Matrix (TLM) method, based on Adapted Radiating Boundaries (ARB). The hybrid ARB method shows a high stability of the algorithm and a very fast computational time. It is especially suitable for the efficient simulation of transient electromagnetic interferences between various lossy structures of complex geometry. The ARB method is applied for the modeling of the e.m. coupling between metallic enclosures. In comparison to the TLM method, the ARB method yields considerable savings in computational effort.

articleTitle: Indirect Measurement of Field Uniformity in TEM Cells Including Cross-Polar Field Components
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: TEM cells are an accepted measurement environment for both emission and immunity measurements. For both cases the field uniformity inside the cell is of importance. Furthermore, theories to correlate TEM cell emission measurements to open area test site (OATS) results assume the field inside the cell to be predominantly vertical. This is not always the case. Longitudinal field components may have a significant influence. Previous methods for measuring the field uniformity use a field sensor in the cell. This paper describes an alternative method to measure the field uniformity and the field components in TEM cells without any connecting cables or optical fibres inside the cell. Using this method not only the vertical but also the longitudinal and horizontal component of the electric field strength inside a GTEM cell are determined. This paper shows that cross-polar coupling in a GTEM cell does exist and the significance of the longitudinal field component at higher frequencies indicates that coupling into higher order modes can occur. Measurements in a GTEM cell are presented and the influence of cross-polar field components is shown.

articleTitle: A MoM/FDTD Hybrid Method for the Evaluation of the EM Fields in Penetrable Objects
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The combination of the marching on in time version of the Method of Moment (MoMTD), and the Finite-Difference in Time Domain (FDTD) technique allows us to develop a new hybrid method to study efficiently the coupling between an antenna and a lossy inhomogeneous dielectric body in its near field region: for example the radiation of a cellular telephone close to a human head. It is essentially based on the equivalence principle and on the iterative solution both for the MoMTD and for the FDTD, realising a perfect matching between the time procedures of the two methods. Numerical and experimental data are presented for a significant situation to validate the model.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on the Radiation from a Bend in a Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to investigate quantitatively the radiation phenomenon from a transmission line with a bend. By using the method of moments, we initially estimate the current distribution, and then we calculate the radiation from a bent transmission line. We first compare our exact solution with the numerical solution by Nakamura et al. (1995) on the assumption of the radiation only from the bend and we come to an excellent agreement. However, the radiation from the whole part of the bent line, suggests that the radiation patterns exhibit a lot of side-lobes, indicating the importance of wave interference from different parts of the line, though the general tendency is the same as in the case of radiation only from the bend. The radiation efficiency is calculated as a function of bend angle, and it is found to be about 10% of the input power for the conventional line height (<<a wavelength).

articleTitle: THE Use of Statistical Signal Processing in EMC
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Statistical signal processing is applied to estimate the geometrical and electrical characteristics of narrowband emissive sources. The key issue of the approach is based upon the use of MUSIC algorithm, which is largely used in array processing in far field conditions, to estimate the positions and the characteristics of emissive sources operating in near field conditions. In view of a practical implementation the MUSIC algorithm is solved by recurring to the Gradient Algorithm to determine the noise subspace eigenvector and to the Genetic Algorithm to maximize the MUSIC spectrum. Suggestions of practical implementations of this theoretical approach related to more complex cases in the area of EMC testing and analysis are also given.

articleTitle: A Lightning Data Survey and Parameters in Retest Criteria
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Currently, many launch vehicle and space vehicle (LV/SV) contractors at Cape Canaveral Air Station (CCAS) use the Cloud-to-Ground Lightning Surveillance System (CGLSS) data to formulate their lightning damage search/retest criteria for launch processing. Consequently, it is very important to understand whether the data can be used effectively to support real-time launch operations. A survey of approximately six years (1/1990 - 10/1995) of lightning data for Space Launch Complexes (SLC)40/41 was conducted. Important CGLSS parameters such as' Peak Lightning Current Amplitudes, Distances from SLC40/41, and Azimuth Angles relative to SLC40/41 were correlated with present lightning damage search criteria. Temporal and seasonal dependence and the flash density were also derived. The survey results reinforce the view that a higher fidelity lightning effects monitoring system, complemented by a more effective lightning damage search (retest) criterion is warranted.

articleTitle: Introducing Height Correction Factors for Accurate Measurements with Biconical Antennas above Groundplane
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The antenna factor of the biconical antenna is a function of antenna height above a ground-plane. Variations in the antenna factor of up to 1.9 dB are observed when the antenna is used in the typical height range of 1 m to 4 m on an open area test site (OATS). The magnitude of this variation depends on the impedance of the antenna balun. From the antenna factor simulations we have derived height correction factors which account for the coupling of biconical antennas above a groundplane. We have demonstrated with antenna calibration measurements what the simulated predictions show. The new method of height correction can be applied to all measurements with biconical antennas, when the balun impedance of the antenna is known. It removes the systematic error caused by the height dependence of the antenna factor. Examples are demonstrated for precision field strength measurements on an OATS, accuracy enhancement for antenna calibration according to the standard site method given in ANSI C63.5 and conversion of OATS antenna factors to free space antenna factors and vice-versa.

articleTitle: Three Dimensional Model for Conductive Enclosures With Apertures and Attached Cables
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This work proposes a Partial Element Equivalent Circuit (PEEC) model for three dimensional conductive enclosures, with apertures, in order to evaluate the spatial distribution of the surface currents, excited by internal harmonic sources, their radiation and their effects on attached cables. The work here also combines the PEEC modeling for the enclosures with the transmission line theory for cables shield. The numerical results are validated by the comparison with measured results on a laboratory mock-up.

articleTitle: A Transient Solution for Nonuniform Multiconductor Transmission Lines in External Fields
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper applies the Time Domain Space Expansion (TDSE) method to the transient simulation of arbitrary Nonuniform Multiconductor Transmission Lines (NMTL) excited by external fields. The discretization scheme is based on a weak formulation obtained by expanding the voltages and currents along the line and the distributed sources due to the incident fields into some trial functions. The projection of the NMTL equations through suitable test functions leads to a linear system of ODE’s, which can be solved with a time integration routine. The method is validated through several numerical examples.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Modeling of the Nerve System
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The role of an equivalent electrical inductance of the nerve membrane in the propagation of the action potential is considered. The high inductance of the nerve fibre membrane results from the inductance of the ionic channels. The totality of the ionic channels, considered as an open oscillating circuit can be represented by an electrical analogue of the nerve fibre membrane. For the propagation of the action potential a nonlinear differential equation with a single wave solution is obtained. Results of numerical calculations based on the proposed model are quoted. Effects of the staedy-state magnetic field on the nerve system can be explained on the basis of the membrane’s electro-dynamical model.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Electromagnetic Shields Using Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The performance analysis of ferromagnetic shields is an "hot topic" in the EMC community, especially in the low frequency range. In this paper the prediction of the magnetic field transmitted through a ferromagnetic shield, in far and near-field conditions, is carried out by means of a neural network based approach. The neural network allows the evaluation of the transmitted field with a good accuracy and 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup> faster than complex numerical models based on FDTD technique or FETD method.. The proposed prediction model has been tested by comparison of the results obtained with the neural network and those evaluated by the FDTD algorithm. The use of a neural network based model is also suitable for the optimization of electromagnetic shields. To this aim in the paper it is computed, as a function of the frequency, the optimal thickness of a Mumetal shield for different values of the incident field in order to reduce the transmitted field below a given threshold.

articleTitle: The Characterisation of Antistatic Materials: An Alternative Approach.
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In the past, the typical characterisation of antistatic materials has been specified by different definitions of resistances, depending on the application of the material. Bulk and surface resistances are specified in standards. Typically for antistatic boxes, a kind of surface resistance is given, including point-to-point measurements. Even recently, IEC standards have been published in this domain. Most of these methods are only related to prevent charging up of materials by their handling. Also, it has been recognised by different researchers that this way of characterising antistatic materials is not correlating with the antistatic behaviour of these materials under practical circumstances. This holds especially for all materials based on a technology of fiber injection in plastics, where the surface resistance is no measure for the overall conductivity of the material. And furthermore, electronic design engineers are not interested in this surface resistance as such, but will ask for the ESD shielding behaviour of an enclosure, in relation with the immunity standard EN 61000-4-2 concerning ESD testing of systems. This paper presents an alternative method of characterising the ESD shielding behaviour of antistatic materials, that can be used for the manufacturing of enclosures. It is based on the recording of a typical ESD discharge in the frequency domain, and by careful analysis of the resulting spectrum. This analysis can be used to rank the materials under test according to an ESD shielding effectiveness. The results will be compared with the results of other measuring methods.

articleTitle: Common-Mode Currents and Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility

authors.preferredName: P. C. T. van der Laan

abstract: Common-mode (CM) currents through cables attached to printed circuit boards (PCB’s) are often the main cause of interference and may even dominate the direct radiation of the board. In this contribution we predict the coupling between the differential-mode (DM) circuit on the board and the CM circuit in a Bersier setup, by means of a rapid transmission-line model. This coupling is expressed as the ratio of the CM current and the DM current. Several boards with different complexity were studied in the frequency domain. For demonstration purposes a board with modern digital electronics was developed. Measurements between 100 kHz - 1 GHz agree with the TL models.

articleTitle: Reducing the Emission of Multi-Layer PCBs by Removing the Supply Plane
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Traditionally multi-layer Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs) have full ground and supply planes. The advantage of multi-layer PCBs for EMC can be increased by removing the full copper power supply plane. Instead the use of power supply tracks is proposed. Power supply decoupling is performed by capacitors between the component supply connection and ground, in combination with ferrite beads or micro chokes in series with the common power supply track to the individual component. In this paper it will be shown that the use of power supply planes leads to unwanted resonances in the PCB, resulting in higher common mode emissions of systems that incorporate multi-layer PCBs.

articleTitle: Studies About Human Electrostatic Discharges
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we report some experimental results we have obtained, dealing with the different waveforms of the human electrostatic discharge (ESD) currents measured for different charging voltages and for different discharge configurations. The wide range of found waveforms, created by a human ESD is presented, discussed and compared to the related waveforms obtained by a commercial ESD simulator. In the final part of the paper it is shown that using the measured values of the starting discharge voltages, a numerical modelling of the ESD can predict the experimental waveform.

articleTitle: Shielding Performance of Power Cables With Low Magnetic Field Emission
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The performance of shields to be used in reducing the magnetic field due to power cables is investigated. The magnetic field is computed either by solving exactly the Helmholtz field equation and by using the approximate solution based on the transmission line approach. The influence of various geometrical and electrical parameters of the cable shield on the shielding effectiveness is assessed. The computed results are compared with measured data. The proposed prediction procedure is a powerful tool for the design of cables with low emission of magnetic field.

articleTitle: On the Key Role of Parasitic Capacitances in the Determination of the Susceptibility to EMI of Integrated Operational Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this work we study the experimental and the simulated behavior of several operational amplifiers subjected to EMI conveyed to their inputs. We analyze, for several bipolar, JFET/bipolar, CMOS and BiCMOS architectures, the currents in all branches of the internal opamp network, including the several parasitics associated to the devices and to the adopted technology and given by EMI conveyed to opamps inputs. In particular, we establish a relation between the values of the non-linear parasitic capacitances in the input stage and the opamp EMI susceptibility to interfering signals of several frequencies. Finally, we devise and successfully implement some guidelines to reduce the susceptibility to EMI of several opamps having standard and advanced CMOS and BiCMOS architectures.

articleTitle: Progress on Modeling EM Interaction With Complex Systems : Applications to Aircraft and Automobiles
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The EM topology method was developed at the end of the 80’s [1 - 4]. Experimental validations performed during the last 2-3 years, have permitted to achieve a significant progress pertaining to the assessment of effects of electromagnetic aggressions on complex systems [5-8].

articleTitle: Reduction of Sar in Human Head by Suppression of Surface Currents Due to a Portable Telephone
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To reduce the spatial peak specific absorption rate (SAR) in the human head, the authors previously proposed attaching a ferrite sheet to a portable telephone. In this paper, its mechanism is investigated by using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) method in conjunction with detailed models of a human head and portable telephone. The findings reveal that the SAR reduction by ferrite sheet attachment is due to the suppression of current flowing on the device surface close to the head. This leads that a low SAR portable telephone can be realized by controlling the current distribution on the device surface.

articleTitle: Development of New Measurement Methods and Limits for EMC Compliance Testing in Smaller Relatively Inexpensive Fully Anechoic Rooms
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The standard site for radiated emission testing in the frequency range 30 MHz to 1 GHz is the 10 m open area test site (OATS). With congestion of the airwaves, testing in the presence of ambient RF interference is increasingly time consuming. This has led to the use of 10 m semi-anechoic rooms (SAR). For operation at frequencies as low as 30 MHz these facilities are expensive. The challenge was to develop limits for a less costly 3 m fully anechoic room (FAR) so that a product has the same probability of complying with the limit as it does for the current limits on a 10 m OATS. New limits need to be set for a FAR because of the absence of a ground plane.

articleTitle: Compensation of Far-End Crosstalk in Interconnects of a Double-Layered Dielectric PCB
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The problem of crosstalk reduction is investigated. Compensation of far-end crosstalk in cascaded sections of coupled inverted microstrip lines and coupled suspended microstrip lines of a double-layered dielectric PCB is considered for case of arbitrary number of sections and arbitrary lengths of the sections. Results of computer simulations of capacitive and inductive couplings are presented. Time-domain far-end crosstalk waveforms are calculated to show an effect of complete far-end crosstalk compensation. A condition of complete compensation is given.

articleTitle: Test Methods for Screening and Balance of Communication Cables
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: With the new triaxial test method all parameters, describing the screening effectiveness of balanced and unbalanced cables, can be measured in one test set-up.

articleTitle: Practical Aspects of EMC in Extended Systems: An Overview
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Extended systems have specific EMC aspects which differ significantly from the EMC aspects of confined electrical or electronic products. This paper reviews the aspects encountered, in practice, in achieving and maintaining EMC of extended systems. In addition, some developments on network systems are noted. These are a special class of extended systems. Finally, this introductory paper summarises the papers presented in this session and relates them as far as is possible to the aspects discussed here.

articleTitle: Properties of the Channel Discharge Function in the Generalized Lightning Travelling Current Source Return Stroke Model
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The properties of the channel discharge function in the generalized lightning travelling current source return stroke model (GTCS) are analyzed. It is shown that the value of the time derivative of the channel discharge function must be equal to zero to avoid discontinuities in the radiated field pattern. Using the GTCS model and the simple model of the channel structure the connection between the channel timedischarge constant and the channel discharge function is derived. Generally taken, the channel time-discharge constant is a function of time and the channel altitude. An example of the possible charge distribution along the channel-base is given enabling the calculation of the channel discharge function and the time-discharge constant. The simple expression connecting the permittivity and the conductivity of the charnel sheath is figured out. All the results are compared with the results previously established for the Traveling Current Source, Diendorfer-Uman and Thottappillil-Uman models.

articleTitle: Propagation of Lightning Generated Electromagnetic Fields Over Finitely Conducting Ground
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper summarises the propagation effects on the lightning generated electric fields and their time derivatives. The mathematics of the problem is outlined and a simple mathematical procedure that can be used to predict the propagation effects is described. The data given in the paper illustrate how the propagation effects influence the peak, the risetime and the half-width of the lightning generated radiation fields and their time derivatives.

articleTitle: Observed Shielding Variations in Cable Assemblies Intended for Differential Signaling of 1.0625 Gigabit/Second Data Rates
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Cable assemblies intended for use in Fibre Channel-like digital data transmission at rates of 1.0625 Gigabit/second were examined for variability in EMI shielding characteristics. Examining three different assemblies, using two different Fibre Channel HSSDC type connectors (with internal printed circuit boards) and one with a more conventional Micro-D Subminiature, connector showed common-mode shield current variations as high as 20 dB from connector to connector for a given cable assembly type. The results also produced a range of absolute levels among cable assembly types spanning 17 dB. The distributions of common-mode currents were broad with standard errors as high 24% of the mean. Radiation was also measured to corroborate findings based on shield current.

articleTitle: Validation Methods for Reverberating Chambers.
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Reverberating chambers are in the final process of becoming tools for official standard. This calls for validation techniques suited to relate them each other. The currently available validation techniques are considered and compared.

articleTitle: A New Generator for Testing of Surge Protection Devices Using Multiple Lightning Current Impulses for Combined Tests With Follow Currents
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new generator for testing of lightning protection equipment is presented. Surge protection devices (SPD's) can be tested according to standards, e.g. [1]. A novelty is the combined test of lightning impulse current and follow current. This test can be performed as a double test in order to simulate the effect of multiple lightning currents on SPD's. The paper deals with the principle of the generator and one test application of a combined tests on a SPD.

articleTitle: Coupled Simulation of Nonlinear Devices and Electromagnetic Effects
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The coupling mechanism is described for a configuration involving a conventional three-dimensional finite difference time domain electromagnetics solver (EMLAB-ISE) and a multidimensional circuit- and semiconductor device simulator (DESSIS-ISE). The time stepping schemes which are different for the two simulators are compared and a correction method is presented which accounts for discontinuous driving currents for the lumped model. Numerical test cases are presented to demonstrate the numerical stability of the coupling mechanism for strongly nonlinear devices and circuits.

articleTitle: Diagnostics of Signal Transmission Lines by Using a Neural Network Based Monitoring of The Radiated Emission
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A two-layer back-propagation NN is trained and used for the diagnostic of faulty load conditions in signal transmission lines above a dissipative plane. The anomaly is detected basing on the monitoring of the amplitude frequency spectra of the radiated EM field, produced by the injection of a voltage pulse at one end of the line. The trained NN is able to distinguish, with an error not greater than 0.5%, among transmission lines of length from 30 cm to 10 m, having matched, open-ended or short-circuit terminations.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Transmission Line Coupling Model With the EFIE Approach for Lightning Induced Overvoltage Prediction
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The transmission line approach, which is commonly used in the power lightning literature for the prediction of lightning induced overvoltage, is compared with the electric field integral equation (EFIE) approach recently introduced by Moini et al. [4], Numerical tests suggest that the two approaches give adequately similar results in the case of simple power lines, and tend to differ from each other as the complexity of the power line geometry increases. This discrepancy can be related to the unacceptable quasi-TEM approximation used in the development of the transmission line approach.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Large Field Simulator by Transient Field Calculations and Measurements
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Large stripline simulators are used for susceptibility tests of large test objects like HV-apparatus, vehicles or even airplanes. The aim of such tests is hardening of electronic devices against fast transients with a high amplitude like high altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulse (HEMP) [4] or very fast transients (VFT’s) caused by switching operations in HV-GIS (gasinsulated switchgear) [3], The test impulses are produced using a special peaking circuit [2]. Measurements have shown that in such a simulator the shape and the rise time of the transient electromagnetic field within the test volume is not the same as it is close to the input of the simulator peaking circuit.

articleTitle: Calculating the Magnetic and Electric Fields Produced by a Line Current Above the Earth
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Electric currents in the ionosphere create magnetic and electric fields that can have an impact on technological systems on the ground such as power systems, pipelines and phone cables. For assessing the geomagnetic hazard to such systems it is necessary to calculate the electric and magnetic fields produced at the earth’s surface by overhead currents. The full solution requires inclusion of the effect of induced currents which are influenced by the conductivity structure of the earth. Considerable progess has been made in this area, both by developing new methods and by adapting methods from other disciplines. We review the computational methods now available which include numerical integration using Fast Fourier Transforms or Fast Hankel Transforms, new series expansions, and the complex image method.

articleTitle: Esprit 23643 (ESDEM) Workshop on ESD Protection Design Methodology
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A new design methodology for ESD protection structures is presented combining advanced TCAD simulation tools and generation of parametrized models for circuit level simulation. Application of this methodology will be presented for smart power and submicron technologies.

articleTitle: An Approach to Production Conformance Testing for Parts of Large Systems
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Ensuring continuing radiated emissions production conformance for large systems is problematical, in that it is often not practical to regularly re-test samples of the whole system. An example of this is with vehicles, which typically have a large number electronic of sub-systems, as test time in chambers suitable for whole vehicle measurements is both rare and expensive. Also if a failure is detected at the system level, no indication is normally given as to what subsystem caused the failure, resulting in a possibly extended “diagnostic” period to locate and fix the problem (during which time products should not be shipped). The approach described in this paper is to use test results from subsystems that have been tested as part of the whole system to define suitable radiated emissions limits for the subsystems, allowing conventional EMI testing to be undertaken on the subsystems as required. The approach required to define this limit is shown to be more complex than might be initially expected, as section 1 shows that radiated emissions measurements have a relatively high variability, and so for example, the approach of just using the initial units actual emissions (perhaps plus a small “safety margin”) as a limit for future tests can cause many false failures.

articleTitle: Integrated Circuit Design for Reduced EMI
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radiation of electromagnetic interference is a problematic side-effect of digital electronic systems. Radiation becomes amplified as it conducts and radiates from an integrated circuit to a PCB and beyond the system. While proficient system level design is paramount for minimizing EMI, the design of the integrated circuits can help to control EMI by minimizing the source of the radiation. Several aspects of typical IC design can be optimized in order to minimize the levels of radiation produce by the device. These aspects include package selection, pin assignments, on-chip module partitioning, power routing, clock distribution, oscillator/clock options, and logic selections.

articleTitle: Measurement of Induced Surges on Telecommunication Subscriber Cables Due to Nearby Lightning Discharge : Basis for Standard Development
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Even though the International Telecommunication Union - Telecommunication Sector (ITU-T) has produced directives that are useful for practising engineers, scientists, researchers, and students with regard to “Resistibility of Telecommunication Equipment to Overvoltages and Overcurrents (RTEOO)” but still total adoption of these directives by the Malaysia telecommunication sector is not justifiable without collecting local data. This is because Malaysia lies in the region where the thunderstorm days are tremendously high. For this, new sets of data on lightning related induced surges are required to produce directives based on Malaysia experience. This paper explains the measurement of lightning induced voltages on real and mock-up telecommunication subscriber cables carried out. The results obtained shall be used for fine tuning of the standards.

articleTitle: An Improved Broad-Band Isotropic E-Field Sensor Using Mach-Zehnder Interferometers
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A broadband electric field sensor integrating sensor elements on Mach-Zehnder interferometers has been developed. The frequency range was raised to 10 GHz by theoretically optimizing the sensor elements. The sensor was fabricated as an isotropic electric field (E-field) sensor having three printed dipole antennas in a mutually orthogonal configuration. Experimental measurements showed high sensitivity of 87 dB(M V/m) (=22mV/m), a wide frequency range, and an ideal directional pattern. The resolution for measuring electric field strength is very high because the sensor elements are very small, 8 mm long.

articleTitle: Equivalent Circuit Models for the Time-Domain Simulation of Ferrite Electromagnetic Wave Absorbers
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper, the reflectivities of various ferrite absorbing structures are analysed in the frequency-domain and Z-transform techniques are applied to develop time-domain models. For flat tiles an equivalent circuit is developed to describe the surface impedance and thus the reflectivity. For grid tiles and wood-backed tiles, the frequency-domain Prony method is used the extract the coefficients of the model from the analytic data. The frequency-domain Prony method is reviewed and the structure of a general discrete time model is described. These methods offer a systematic and general approach to the modelling of reflectivity functions in transmission-line modelling (TLM) or the modelling of surface impedance functions in the finite-difference timedomain (FDTD) method. Results are presented comparing the reflectivity performance of the models with analysis. Finally, the performance of a practical anechoic chamber modelled using this approach is compared with measurements.

articleTitle: Combined Modelling of ICs, Packages and PCBs using Analytical Equivalent-Circuit Approximations
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The construction is demonstrated of equivalent-circuit models, describing PCB lay-out, IC-chips and packages. The effect of external cables is taken into account by including common-mode signals in the model. For electromagnetic compatibility, this enables the description of the complete coupling path from chip to outside world. A comparison is given between analytical and numerical methods to construct the equivalent circuits and a newly derived analytical result is presented for the magnetic coupling from differential-mode to common-mode signals on a PCB.

articleTitle: An Approach to Protect Civil Systems From the Adverse Effects of High Power Electromagnetic (HPE) Environments.
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: High Power Electromagnetic (HPE) Environments are electromagnetic radiated and conducted environments that are induced through different means. The term "high power" here does not apply to the source generating the disturbances, but rather the level of the environments illuminating a system. This paper will review the different classes of transient and continuous sources that may be considered in this definition and will also review the levels of fields that have been known to cause serious problems with civil systems. The paper will also review the EMC and EMP standards being produced by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and will propose an approach to deal with newer threats that have developed in the past few years.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Propagation and Radiation of a Twisted-Pair Transmission Line Using the Non-orthogonal FDTD Technique (NFDTD)
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper the broadband propagating and radiating properties of a twisted pair-transmission line are studied. This is accomplished by defining a coordinate system which conforms to the twisted wire geometry and subsequently solving Maxwell’s equations in this general curvilinear coordinate system. Several new techniques were employed in this work. Specifically, the surface impedance boundary condition, the lumped source/load, and the near-field to far-field transformation were each applied in general curvilinear coordinates.

articleTitle: Mode-Stirred Chamber as Test Facility for Electromagnetic Susceptibility Measurements
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper presents the characteristics and usage of a mode-stirred chamber for electromagnetic susceptibility (EMS) measurement. It will be shown how the field inside the chamber is distributed and which degree of field homogeneity is achievable. The structure of the stirrer and its characteristics will be presented. A set-up for EMS testing in the mode-stirred chamber is displayed. The results of the susceptibility measurement of different measurement techniques will be compared to results obtained in an anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Determination of the Uncertainty of the Radiated EMI Predicted by Measuring the Absolute Value of a Magnetic Near Field
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Uncertainty of prediction of radiated EMI of small equipment by means of the measurement of magnetic near field is investigated theoretically in the frequency range 30 - 960 MHz. In this paper a comprehensive set of different EUTs is constructed by means of two dipole moments. Each dipole moment combination thus characterises the radiation properties of one possible EUT. Different combinations are constructed by placing two dipole moments to a number of different polarisations and locations within the volume of the EUT. Dipole moment type may be electric or magnetic. Also the phase difference of the dipole moments is varied. Far field produced by each dipole moment combination is predicted using three different near-field to far-field transformations. Predicted far field in proportion to the real far field is computed, and PDFs of the far-field prediction accuracy are presented.

articleTitle: Simulation of Coupling to Underground Cables Caused by Higher Frequency Components of Power Line Transients
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The use of the circuit simulation package SPICE (Simulation Program with Integral Circuit Emphasis) permits the complex analysis of the EMI (electromagnetic interference) in underground cables. In the paper the SPICE has been applied for the simulation of voltages between sheath and cable conductor due to excitation of the cable by higher frequency components of power line transients. The cable has been modelled as the large multinode electrical equivalent circuit containing active and passive elements. The voltage between the cable conductor and the cable sheath is produced by a driving voltage controlled voltage source. The example of calculation of voltages and potentials produced by higher frequency components of power line transients in the inductively influenced cable has been presented in the papers. The SPICE simulation constitutes an alternative and convenient approach to solution of the problem of coupling to underground cables due to harmonics of power line transients when comparing with both the frequency domain and the time domain solutions.

articleTitle: Analysis and Experimental Validation of the Shielding Performances of Complex Chiroshields for EMC Applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The shielding performances of complex chiroshields - shielding structures where chiral materials and wire-meshes have been introduced - are here predicted, computed and finally measured. The electromagnetic problem has been rephrased in terms of circuit theory through an equivalent circuit network model properly introduced by a spectral tecnique. The spectral formalism yields an accurate expression of the surface impedance of this type of shield, and the shielding effectiveness of the structure has been computed in a closed form. The analitical predictions have been compared with numerical simulations and with experimental measurements of the shielding effectiveness of properly designed shielding samples. The obtained results show the interesting shielding properties of these structures, promising for EMC applications.

articleTitle: Studying Positive Lightning Induced Effects on a Very Close Power Distribution Line
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Adopting a simple model in which the discharge is represented by an equivalent electrical network, we determine the whole positive lightning discharge instantaneous parameters such as the current, the velocity, the electromagnetic fields, ... The effects induced by a very close lightning on a 500 m power distribution line are also characterised. It is shown that for the distances that we considered, the leader electric fields change contribute significantly to the amplitude and wave shape of the induced voltages and could operate some lightning protection devices before the return stroke.

articleTitle: The Combined Use of FEM and IEM for Predicting Crosstalk in Transmission Unes
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two-dimensional analysis is currently used in the EMC problem such as microstrip lines, crosstalk etc. However, there have been reported very few reports on the quantitative analysis for any kind of complicated structures. In this paper we propose a combined use of finite element method (FEM) and infinite element method (IEM) in the analysis of microstrip lines with any arbitrary configurations with any values of strip width, strip spacing, its height etc, and we investigate quantitatively the crosstalk phenomena of transmission lines. Also, the crosstalk phenomena with taking into account the effect of the finite-sized ground plane, have been investigated numerically and experimentally.

articleTitle: Simulated Behaviour of Fully Anechoic Rooms for Measurement of Radiated Emissions
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The possibility of using fully anechoic rooms (FAR) instead of open area test sites (OATS) for radiated emission measurements have been studied using simulation techniques and ideal models of the test sites. A validation of the technique using real measurements showed excellent agreement. The simulations show that a 3 m FAR is a good alternative for emissions measurement on most EUT:s and avoid some problems seen on an OATS due to the ground plane reflections.

articleTitle: Introduction to GTD and its Combination with MOM
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Geometrical Theory of Diffraction General Remarks 1. Using the method of subsections within the Method of Moments restricts the size of objects which can be investigated. Usually a maximum length for a subsection (in case of patches for a base line) of λ/10 is specified (λ = wavelength). 2. Depart from the fact that the system matrix becomes larger and larger with increasing frequency the matrix becomes more and more ill-conditioned. 3. In 1962 Mr. Keller introduced the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction. The idea is that at high frequencies the electromagnetic field can be described sufficiently by a limited number of rays. 4. The Geometrical Theory of Diffraction represents an extension of the classical theory of geometrical optics. 5. It permits the calculation of high-frequency fields in the vicinity of electrically large and complex bodies. By applying variational techniques asymtotic solutions of Maxwell’s equations can be found. 6. Additionally to the well-known reflection process on the surface of a metallic body the geometrical theory of diffraction uses three more processes: 1. rays, diffracted at edges between surfaces 2. creeping waves 3. rays, diffracted at tips and wedges. GTD = Geometrical Theory of Diffraction UTD = Uniform Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (Both expressions will be used interchangeably!)

articleTitle: On-Site Measurements and Mitigation of Emissions from a Telecom Central Office
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The author has previously described several practical measurement techniques for performing on-site EMC measurements [1], [2], [3], This paper will detail a very unique interference investigation, from initial receipt of a complaint to satisfactory mitigation of the interference. This paper explains how measurements were made of radiated emissions from a working telephone central office, to verify that the levels of emissions were below the United States legal limits and to ensure that interference to an adjacent radio amateur was not due to noncompliance of the telecom equipment. After showing that the signal levels were below the legal limits, the paper then describes some simple, easily tested, temporary on-site shielding techniques that were tried, and the actual techniques that were ultimately used to reduce the emissions that were received by the amateur radio operator by several dB.

articleTitle: A Generalised View of the Problem of EMC for Cathode Ray Tubes
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Cathode ray tubes of different types are still used for image display, information input-output processes and so on. This paper is dedicated to the attempt of generalisation of different factors which have to be taken into account for the problem “cathode ray tube - electromagnetic compatibility” (in wide sense) consideration. The factors are divided into two groups - constant and casual. Short characteristics of the factors are given. Two sides of the problem are discussed: influence óf environment on CRT and influence of CRT on environment - equipment and man.

articleTitle: Transients on Secondary Equipment in Medium Voltage Switchgear Installations
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Conventional current and voltage transformers of medium voltage distribution switchgear are going to be technologically replaced by modem low-power sensors. In order to ensure their undisturbed operation in future applications fundamental investigations have to be done about the electromagnetic stress to which sensors are supposed. Measurements of transients on the secondary lines to transformers in general and particularly to the sensors as well as on the primary circuit were performed for typical switching actions. Corresponding results of the transient voltages and of the transmitting behaviour of transformers and sensors are presented. A kind of transfer function is introduced in order to describe the transmitting behaviour of the sensors and transformers also in the frequency domain.

articleTitle: Capacitive Voltage Probe for Non-Contact Measurement of Common-Mode Voltage
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Capacitive voltage probe is described that can measure the common-mode voltage on a cable without touching its conductor. This capacitive voltage probe has with two coaxial electrodes; the inner electrode works as a voltage pickup, and the outer one shields the inner electrode. These electrodes separate into two parts for clamping to the cable. Using a high input impedance circuit, this probe measures the common-mode voltage by detecting the voltage difference between the two electrodes . The probe’s characteristics were evaluated by measuring its linearity and frequency response. The results show that this probe has a dynamic range of 100 dB and flat frequency response from 10 kHz to 30 MHz. Errors in measurement due to the position of the clamped cable in the inner electrode and to differences in the cable radius were evaluated theoretically and experimentally. The results indicate that the influence of the cable position is small and the deviation in sensitivity induced by differences in the cable radius can be calibrated using compensatory data.

articleTitle: EMC Control in the New Industrial Environment
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Using real cases taken from life experience, we present In this tutorial how ‘the job today’ of an EMC engineer can profit of last prediction techniques and numerical models. The aim is to provide correct prediction, clear evidence and in-time answers for the identified VICTIM.

articleTitle: Response of Shielded Cables to an External Electromagnetic Field Excitation. Modeling and Experimental Validation†)
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Two methods for the calculation of internal responses of shielded cables submitted to an external impulse electromagnetic field are analyzed. One is the classical frequency-domain approach, the second is a new mixed frequency-time-domain model, which uses a link to a well-known transient analysis code. This last feature makes possible the application of the second model to complex networks with several branches. In both models, measured values of the cable transfer impedance values have been used. The comparison between internal currents and voltages calculated with both models and measurements using an EMP simulator shows a reasonable good agreement. These comparisons validate the analyzed models and in particular the new combined frequency-time domain approach.

articleTitle: The Measurement and Use of Free-Space Antenna Factors in EMC Applications
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Antenna gain is usually assumed to be independent of the antenna surroundings. In theory this is taken to be the case also in EMC measurements, but current practice is that neither the EUT nor the antenna factor are measured in free-space conditions, resulting in errors in antenna factor of about ±1.5 dB. Though this may be small compared to the total uncertainty of an EMC measurement, it carries an importance of its own when it tips an emission measurement above the limit and when it causes an anechoic chamber to fail its NSA test. The use of free-space antenna factor is a sound basis from which to quantify antenna related uncertainties of measurement.

articleTitle: Esprit ESDEM Open Meeting ESD Protection Design Methodology
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Open Meeting on the ESPRIT Project ESDEM (Electrostatic Discharge Protection Design Methodology), a European Union Information Technology R&D Project In this workshop a general overview will be given of the state of the art, future requirements and development trends with respect to the design of ESD structures considering submicron MOS processes. The material discussed in two invited papers, 3 contributed papers and 10 posters represents a selection of the ongoing research in the design of ESD protection devices and circuits. A new design methodology for ESD structures is presented combining advanced TCAD simulation tools and extraction of ESD models leading to circuit level simulation. The software demonstrations reflect results and applications of the project.

articleTitle: Application of New Spline-Based Expansion and Weighting Functions for the Analysis of Complex Thin-Wire Structures
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: An analysis of thin-wire antennas and scatterers using orthogonal spline-based expansions is presented. So-called B-splines are introduced as a generalisation of the rectangular and triangle expansion functions. A procedure is described for obtaining special spline-based functions which incorporate the continuity equation at junctions of wires into expansions. It is clearly shown, that the expansion functions used increase the number of expansions near the junctions of the wires automatically. The thin-wire version of the electric-field integral equation (EFIE) is solved by the Method of Moments (MoM) using Galerkin’s method. Two numerical examples are provided, which fully take advantage of the symmetry of the resulting matrix.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of EMC Tests for Compliance
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of numerical simulation of Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) tests for compliance. The experimental setups for conducted emissions and radiated emissions tests are analyzed and modeled. The final goal is an approximate prediction of the EMC characteristics of an electric/electronic system, as experimentally measured by the proper setup specified by the regulations. EMC prediction based on this approach gives rise to new computer-based learning tools for students, that can be also of some help to designers, experienced in electronics, but with curricula which do not explicitly address EMC.

articleTitle: High-Frequency Methods for EM Couplings in Complex Environments
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Overcrowded platforms are often subjected to electromagnetic coupling between antennas and/or apparatuses operating close to each other. For these problems, a rigorous full-wave analysis based on the solution of integral or differential equations becomes computationally prohibitive for increasing frequency or for large-band investigations, thus making useful and sometimes inevitable to resort to high- frequency techniques. The development and applications of these techniques have mainly been based on two leading theories, namely the Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (GTD) [1] and the Physical theory of Diffraction (PTD) [2]. Both of them make use of solutions of local canonical problems, that in most practical instances have an infinite, uniform cylindrical configuration. These canonical problems are used by GTD to provide an estimate of a diffracted ray field contribution, and by PTD to find an estimate of the currents that should be introduced to correct those predicted by the Physical Optics (PO). The GTD leads to a very attractive picture of the scattering from a complex object, in terms of rays emanating from isolated "flash points". Unfortunately, searching for the relevant "flash points" in a complex environment is not at all a straightforward matter. The singularities that occur in the original GTD formulation at the shadow boundaries (SB) of the Geometrical Optics (GO) field have been removed by its uniform versions, such as the Uniform Geometrical Theory of Diffraction (UTD) [3] In the UTD framework, some canonical configurations have been recently investigated; among these: vertices [4], thick edges [5], skew edges [6] periodic surfaces [7], loaded structures [8], circular cylinders [9],[10]. The objective of these investigations is the development of uniform diffraction coefficients for the synthesis of various wave diffraction processes. In this paper, after an overview on the leading high- frequency theories [l]-[3], the use of the new canonical diffraction coefficients derived in [4]-[10] will be discussed in the frame of EM coupling applications in complex environments. Particular emphasis will be given to the engineering solutions for reducing interference between antennas e/o apparatuses by using polarisation-independent corrugated screens [11]. Finally, the limitations of the ray methods close to and at caustics will be discussed, and the main methods to overcome this limitations will be addressed, focusing the attention on the Incremental Theory of Diffraction [12][13].

articleTitle: Effects of Connecting Hardware and Terminals on the Screening, Crosstalk and Transmission Properties of an Over 100 MHz Datalink
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Current copper based balanced data cables achieve extremely high symmetry and transmission performances. This factor together with the ever increasing frequencies, means that the so called connecting hardware (CHW), in spite of their short lengths of only a few centimetres, create the bottle neck for increasing the bandwidth of open data cablings into the hundreds of MHz. The studies presented in this paper show that CHW can no more be regarded electrically short and that special care must be taken immediately to improve its crosstalk performances by choosing a new mechanically symmetrical connecting interface structure, in which no systematic couplings are present. Additional care must be taken so as to ensure that the EM screening is sufficiently tight and reliable at joints, and that the characteristic impedances of CHW and cable do not differ by more than about 30 % of the corresponding return loss at high frequencies of about 17 dB.

articleTitle: Signal Integrity and Behavioral Models of Digital Devices
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The behavioral modeling of digital integrated circuits is becoming an important resource for the simulations of large and critical digital circuits. In this paper, we address the behavioral modeling of CMOS integrated circuit on the basis of the In- put/output Buffer Information Specification (IBIS). The aim of this work is to provide guidelines to build executable models from IBIS data, which is not provided by the IBIS specification itself. Such an ability is of paramount importance for the validation of IBIS data sets through the comparison of measured transient responses of digital devices and the corresponding responses obtained by IBIS models. Besides discussing basic elements of IBIS models and their critical points, we propose an effective IBIS model, which offers improved accuracy and efficiency, and can be effectively exploited for experimental validations.

articleTitle: A Discrete Transfer Function Model for the Timedomain Calibration Data of EMP Sensors
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Accurate measurement of electromagnetic pulse requires the knowledge of the response characteristics of measuring system to pulsed signals. Conventional time-domain or frequency-domain calibration method only provides the sensitivity of the sensors. This kind of information can not describe the pulse response of the measuring system directly and completely. A discrete transfer function model is used here to describe the time-domain and frequency-domain characteristics of the EMP sensors. By using the time history obtained from time-domain calibration, the model of the sensor is established by system identification approach. From the model parameters, sensitivity in each frequency band and the intrinsic frequency of the sensor can be calculated directly. Further application of this method can also give a satisfactory compensation of the measuring system.

articleTitle: Macro-Elements for Accurate Dispersive Modeling of Thin Material Sheets and Impedance Boundary Conditions in FDTD
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A novel methodology is presented for the development of special macroelements for accurate modeling of both thin material sheets of subcell thickness and dispersive impedance boundary conditions, in the context of the Finite-Difference Time-Domain method. Such macro-elements help expedite the numerical solution of a variety of electromagnetic boundary-value problems associated with the electromagnetic compatibility assessment of systems involving electrically large surfaces covered by thin conducting foils and/or composite dielectric sheets.

articleTitle: Mains Simulation Network (LISN or AMN) Uncertainty - How Good are Your Conducted Emission Measurements?
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: This paper provides a practical method of estimating worst-case measurement uncertainty for conducted emission measurements using artificial mains simulation networks. It is shown that without special care, the AMN impedance error may be nearly ±6 dB at the worst-case frequency of 30 MHz. Even at the best case frequency of 150 kHz, the AMN impedance error may reach an amount between 2 dB and 4 dB. Just for the impedance errors, the worst-case AMN error at 30 MHz contributes a standard uncertainty of ≈3.5 dB to the combined standard uncertainty for conducted emission measurement. A simple, practical method is given for reducing the impedance errors, and bringing their related uncertainty contributions to less than 1 dB.

articleTitle: Microwave Interaction With a Personal Computer: Experiment and Modeling
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we present both experimental and numerical modeling results for the microwave interaction with and upset of a typical Personal Computer (PC) system. For the experimental investigation, a PC running a popular spreadsheet package was exposed to microwave energy in the frequency range of 1-4 GHz. The experiments were conducted inside an anechoic chamber using a stepped-frequency microwave generator. A wideband horn antenna was used as the radiator and the frequency was stepped from the lowest frequency to the highest while the operation of the PC was monitored. Simple, but computationally intensive, hard-disk read-write operations were being executed by the PC. Various polarizations and angles of incidence of the radiation were tested. Disruption of the PC occurred at several distinct frequencies, but not for all polarizations, which are believed to be the resonant frequencies of the PC enclosure. In order to confirm this, the finite difference time domain (FDTD) technique was used to model the coupling on a simplified geometry of the problem. The modeling results confirm that indeed the coupling to various printed circuit board (PCB) lines placed inside the enclosure occurs predominantly at certain frequencies associated with the resonant frequencies of the PC enclosure. The predicted coupling is also found to vary considerably with the polarization of the incident field.

articleTitle: Evaluation of the Coupling into Cables Through Shield Discontinuities
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: To determine the shielding effectiveness of a cable it is nesessary to be aware of discontinuities within the shield. These might result from imperfections such as an improper installation of the cable at its ends, inhomogenous sections of a braided shield or connecting devices. In this paper, a new method to characterize these imperfections is presented. This is achieved by combining experimental measurements with the method of moments and the transmission line theory. The resulting model of the discontinuity is derived from the transmission line model of a shielded cable. By using the same test fixture for determining the coupling parameters of a coaxial cable, the properties of the discontinuities are evaluated and displayed. Finally, the application of the obtained coupling parameters to EMC analysis is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Physical Mechanisms of High-Frequency Electromagnetic Field Generation by a Lightning Discharge
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Relations between parameters of Lightning discharge at the leader phase and return stroke phase are obtained. It is shown that the high-frequency radiation of Lightning is determined by the parameters of the streamer zone of a leader at the final jump phase. Methods for determination of Lightning parameters from the measurements of statistical properties of electromagnetic field are proposed. The influence of random bending and branching of Lightning channel on the characteristics of electromagnetic field in far field zone is considered. New quantitative characteristics for analysis of electromagnetic field of Lightning are introduced.

articleTitle: Comparison of Couplers Used for Cable Injection in Commercial and Military Susceptibility Tests: Capacitive Versus Inductive Coupling Methods
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Military and Commercial EMC Standards specify conducted immunity test that use bulk cable and single lead injection test techniques. These requirements have similar test objectives and techniques. However, comparisons of the test results are not possible without an understanding of the various coupler characteristics. These Standards require either a capacitive coupler/clamp (EN61000-4-4), an inductive coupler or injection probe (MIL-STD-462D test methods CS114, CS115, and CS116 and DO-160C Section 20 & 22) or a coupling/decoupling network (discrete capacitors per EN61000-4-12). This paper discusses and compares the coupling efficiency of these various coupling devices through measurement of the normalized test signal energy at the load and source ends of different circuit/line configurations and coupling of the test signal onto a single line and a bulk cable. The study recommendations: i) use inductive coupling device for fast transients/burst; ii) use inductive coupling device for both 100 kHz and 1 MHz ring (damped oscillatory) waveform; and iii) study further the damped sine waveform coupling efficiency using a 5-10 MF discrete capacitor with a decoupling LISN to determine its adequacy for both MIL-STD-461 and EN 61000-4-12.

articleTitle: Exact Determination of Resonant Frequencies in TEM Cells
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: A basic limitation to the usable bandwidth of a TEM cell is the occurance of resonances of higher order modes which disturb the desired field distribution. Approximate expressions for resonant frequencies are known in the literature [5]. These expressions are based on empirically determined values for the effective length of the cell. In this paper the mechanism of wave propagation is considered from the viewpoint of mode matching methods. An analytical solution for the resonant frequencies in a GTEM cell is presented. The solution is exact for the first few resonances because for these the influence of the absorbers can be neglected. Calculated resonances are compared to measurements.

articleTitle: Generalization of the BLT Equation
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The response of a multiconductor transmission line network to electromagnetic excitation is described by the BLT equation. This paper generalizes the BLT equation to include nonuniform multiconductor transmission lines in two different ways. This allows one to model quite general electromagnetic systems in the topological formalism of the BLT equation.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Field Coupling to an Electrically Small Antenna in a Rectangular Cavity
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this paper we develop a method to estimate analytically the current induced in an electrically small loaded antenna in a rectangular cavity with perfectly conducting walls. The method is similar to the small range potential method in quantum mechanics [1], A solution for the induced current on the scatterer inside the resonator has the same form as the current induced on the same scatterer in the free space multiplied by a constant. The value of this constant is determined by the regularized cavity Green's function at the antenna location and the scattering amplitude of a small antenna in free space. The result obtained gives the possibility of analytically estimating the frequency dependence of the induced current and the mutual coupling for wiring elements inside cavities. At the end of this paper, possible applications of this method are discussed.

articleTitle: The Effects of Cell Size on FDTD Calculations for Cubic Structures.
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: When defining a model for use with the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method, it is necessary to discretise the problem into rectilinear cells. The size of these cells has an effect on the numerical results. This paper quantifies these effects experimentally, using metallic, cubic structures. The results justify the use of a λ/10 cell size, giving <3dB variation. These results also show little gain in using smaller cell sizes than this. An interpolation method is introduced to enhance the FDTD calculations, allowing cell sizes as large as λ/5 to be used, thereby reducing computation time and resource requirements.

articleTitle: Uncertainties in Standardized EMC Compliance Testing
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: In this tutorial part of the workshop ‘Uncertainties in EMC compliance testing’ it will be discussed how to approach uncertainties in standardized EMC compliance testing such that it can be justified to introduce an uncertainty margin in the compliance criterion of a test. It will be shown that the use of EMC measurement uncertainty margins, as advocated by many accreditation bodies today, cannot serve that purpose. Marked differences between metrology and EMC measurements will be identified. The approach, which puts part of the burden on the standard drafters and part on the test houses, will be elucidated by examples of actual conducted and radiated emission and immunity testing, including approaches to quantify or reduce the uncertainty contributions. Progress made by IEC/CISPR/A will be reported. Uncertainty studies must lead to the improvement of EMC standards and to procedures to judge quantitatively the capabilities of an EMC test house. They will also lead to a justifiable application of uncertainties in the compliance criterion, when needed.

articleTitle: The Dependence of the Leader and Return Stroke Field Changes on the Orientation of a Segment of the Leader Channel
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The total leader field change and the ratio of that to the total return stroke field change, between 1 and 20 km, were calculated for leader channels of which a section of the upper part is oriented at different angles. These two parameters significantly vary with the angle of inclination of the oriented part. The charge source height deduced from the total leader field change to return stroke field change ratio vary in a broad range of values when the angle of inclination of even a small channel segment is changed. These results explain the scatter of the total leader field change and the ratio of that to the total return stroke field change observed in previous studies. The total charge drained in to the leader channel is inaccurate to be deduced by the total leader field change without taking in to account the geometry of the channel. These results raise doubts on the applicability of the total leader field change to return stroke field change ratio, based on the straight leader channel model, in validating return stroke models.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Printed Circuit Boards under EMC-Constraints
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: The design of modern-day microelectronic systems is confronted by challenges due to growing system complexity, higher operating speed as well as trend towards a more compact design. Additionally one faces an increasing economical pressure to integrate components and subsystems to highly compact systems with likewise high operating speeds.

articleTitle: Spectrum Management/ Utilization and Wireless Telecommunications
publicationTitle: 13th International Zurich Symposium and Technical Exhibition on Electromagnetic Compatibility
abstract: Radio has become indispensable for our society to function, but spectrum scarcity hampers its development. This text discusses various aspects related to the use and management/ regulation of the radio frequency spectrum resources. It gives an insight into field of research of Working Group El "Spectrum Management/Utilization and Wireless Telecommunications" of International Union of Radio Science (URSI). Note. The opinions expressed are the author’s personal views, and do not engage any entity.
